# Turn your Zoom call into meeting minutes in 5 minutes with Grok

You just finished a Zoom call and need minutes fast. Instead of typing for half an hour, you can get help from Grok to create a concise summary. Here’s how.

## Before you start
- A **Zoom cloud recording** you can access (or the transcript from it).
- A **free xAI account** (Grok is free to use).
- A **computer or phone** with a web browser.
- Roughly **5 minutes** of your time.
- A **text editor** or email app to paste the minutes.

> Grok can't send the minutes for you — you'll copy and share them yourself.

## Step 1 — Get your Zoom recording or transcript
Open the Zoom website or app and go to **Recordings**. Find the call you want.
If available, download the **transcript** (.vtt or .txt file) — this gives Grok the text it needs to work with.
If no transcript is available, you can play the recording and take notes yourself, then use those notes in the next step.
You'll know it worked when you have a text file or written notes with the key points from the call.

💬 Example:
Open the recording for "Team Sync" and click **More** > **Download transcript** if available.

## Step 2 — Open Grok and start a new chat
Go to [grok.com](https://grok.com) in your browser and sign in with your xAI account. Tap **New chat** or click the plus icon to begin a fresh conversation.
You'll see a blank chat window with a text box at the bottom.
After you click New chat, a new conversation opens and you can type your first message.
If you don't see New chat, look for a button like **Start a new chat** or a plus symbol.
You'll know it worked when the chat window is empty and ready for your prompt.

💬 Example:
Type nothing yet — just leave the chat empty for the next step.

## Step 3 — Ask Grok to write minutes from your notes or transcript
If you have a Zoom transcript file: copy the text and paste it into Grok's chat box.
If you took your own notes: paste those instead.
Then type your prompt:

💬 Example:
"Please write concise meeting minutes from these notes. Include key decisions, action items with owners, and next steps. Keep it under 200 words."

Grok processes your text and generates the minutes.
After you send the prompt, Grok creates the summary.
If nothing happens, try refreshing the page and starting a new chat.
You'll know it worked when Grok displays a formatted set of minutes.

## Step 4 — Review and polish the minutes
When Grok finishes, read the minutes it generated. If anything is missing or unclear, reply:
"Add the name of the project we discussed and the deadline for the next milestone."
Grok displays the updated minutes in the same chat.
After you send the follow-up, Grok revises the text and shows the new version.
If Grok doesn't change the text, try rephrasing your request ("Include the project name and deadline in the minutes.").
You'll know it worked when the updated minutes appear in the chat.

💬 Example:
"Add the name of the project we discussed and the deadline for the next milestone."

## Step 5 — Copy and share the minutes
Highlight the minutes text in the chat, press **Cmd+C** (Mac) or **Ctrl+C** (Windows), and paste them into your email, Slack, or document. Add a subject line like "Minutes from 5 June sync" and send.
You'll see the minutes in a text box in your chat.
After you copy the text, you can paste it anywhere you need.
If the text doesn't copy, try selecting it again or right-clicking and choosing Copy.
You'll know it worked when the minutes appear in your email or chat app exactly as you pasted them.

💬 Example:
Subject: Minutes from 5 June sync
Body: Please find the minutes below.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** Pasting too little information for Grok to work with.
  **Fix:** Include your full notes or transcript — the more context Grok has, the better the minutes.

- **Mistake:** Asking Grok to write minutes without specifying the format.
  **Fix:** Always include "key decisions, action items with owners, and next steps" in your prompt so the output is useful.

- **Mistake:** Forgetting to review the minutes before sharing.
  **Fix:** Read the draft once, then ask Grok to add anything missing — it's faster than rewriting yourself.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** After any quick catch-up, turn your notes into minutes in minutes instead of typing for half an hour.
- **For your business or work:** Share clear, concise notes with your team right after the call, so everyone knows what to do next.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with one call this week and see how much time you save.

## Try it now
Open your Zoom recordings, get your transcript or notes, and paste them into Grok. Ask it to write concise minutes — you'll have the first draft in under two minutes.
